content.text:
Fixed. The bug in `src/launcher.mjs` was that `existsSync` only checked the path existed, not that it was actually a runnable script — a plugin path pointing at a directory (or, on non-root systems, an unreadable file) got handed straight to `bash`, which failed with its own exit code (e.g. `126`) and a generic bash diagnostic instead of a clean `REFUSED` (exit `2`) naming the plugin. Spawn failures (interpreter couldn't even launch) were also silently swallowed into exit `2` with no stderr message at all.

Changes in `src/launcher.mjs`:
- Before spawning, verify the script `statSync`s as a regular file and passes an `accessSync(R_OK)` check — refuse (exit 2, `plugin <name> cannot be run` on stderr) without ever invoking bash if not.
- Check `spawnSync`'s `run.error` (interpreter couldn't be launched) and refuse the same way.
- Treat `run.status === null` (no exit code, e.g. killed before exiting) as a refusal too.
- A plugin that actually starts still has its own exit code returned untouched (verified `hello` → `0`, `fails` → `7` still pass).

Added tests in `test/launcher.test.mjs` for: a plugin path that's a directory, the refusal message naming the plugin, and a case where the interpreter itself can't be launched — confirming no output is produced (the plugin never started). Added a `plugins/isdir.sh/` directory fixture to back the directory test. All 6 tests pass.
